subDimensions.name: Mission, theory of change and target segment

mapping.gapPattern: Leaders describe the ESO as serving 'all SMEs', the theory of change lives only inside funder proposals, and the enterprises selected drift away from the intended segment.
mapping.diagnosis: The organisation has not agreed whom it serves and what should change for them, so programmes, selection and reporting pull in different directions.
mapping.prescription: Agree a one sentence target statement, draw a one page theory of change with assumptions, and write the target segment into selection criteria and reporting.

intervention.resources: Facilitated leadership workshop, theory of change template, segment definition sheet

measurement.kpi: Share of enterprises supported in the period that fit the written target segment
measurement.baselineMethod: Client database extract compared with the written segment definition
measurement.provisionalTarget: 75 percent or more fit within six months

mapping.gapPattern: Curriculum is copied from foreign or funder templates, programme length and cohort size follow the grant budget, and entrepreneurs only meet staff or mentors one to one.
mapping.diagnosis: Programme design was inherited rather than chosen, so content may not fit Ghanaian sectors, languages or the stage of the enterprises served.
mapping.prescription: Review each module with local entrepreneurs and sector practitioners, write down why length, cohort size and intensity were chosen, and build scheduled peer sessions into every cohort.

intervention.resources: Curriculum review template, local case study bank, peer session facilitation guide

measurement.kpi: Share of curriculum modules revised with documented local input
measurement.baselineMethod: Module list compared with consultation records
measurement.provisionalTarget: 80 percent of modules reviewed within six months

mapping.gapPattern: New programmes are designed when a funder call appears, there is no needs assessment from entrepreneurs, and leaders cannot say who else serves the same enterprises.
mapping.diagnosis: Demand is assumed from funder priorities rather than tested, which risks duplicating other providers and offering what entrepreneurs do not value.
mapping.prescription: Run a short needs assessment with target entrepreneurs before each new design, map other providers in the region, and estimate the size of the target segment and the share reached.

intervention.resources: Needs assessment questionnaire, provider mapping template, segment sizing sheet

measurement.kpi: Number of programmes designed with a written needs assessment in the last 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of programme design files against needs assessments
measurement.provisionalTarget: Every new programme designed with a needs assessment

mapping.gapPattern: The strategic plan is a funding concept note, the delivery model sits in founders' heads, and expansion follows funding offers without a capacity check.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO depends on a few people and cannot show it could grow, replicate or hand over without losing quality.
mapping.prescription: Write a three year plan with measurable targets, document the delivery model as an operating manual, and add a capacity check before every expansion decision.

intervention.resources: Strategy planning workshop, operating manual template, capacity check form

measurement.kpi: Share of core delivery processes documented in an operating manual
measurement.baselineMethod: Checklist of selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data processes
measurement.provisionalTarget: Core processes documented within six months

mapping.gapPattern: Selection relies on personal contact or one decision maker, rejected applicants are not recorded, and most participants were already supported elsewhere.
mapping.diagnosis: Selection cannot be defended or analysed, and the programme may be serving the easiest enterprises rather than those who most need support.
mapping.prescription: Publish criteria, use a two reviewer scoring sheet, keep a register of every applicant with reasons, and run a baseline diagnostic and support plan for each selected enterprise.

intervention.resources: Selection scoring sheet, applicant register template, baseline diagnostic form

measurement.kpi: Share of selected enterprises scored by two or more reviewers
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of scoring sheets for the last round
measurement.provisionalTarget: 100 percent of selections scored by two reviewers

mapping.gapPattern: Support time goes mainly to pitch decks, mentors are matched by availability, feedback forms are not analysed, and market access is left to chance.
mapping.diagnosis: Delivery is driven by the standard curriculum rather than by what entrepreneurs need most, so mentoring and market linkage add less value than they could.
mapping.prescription: Collect and rank needs at entry, match mentors using written assessments, analyse feedback every cohort, and plan named market access activities with buyers.

intervention.resources: Needs ranking form, mentor matching sheet, feedback analysis template, buyer engagement plan

measurement.kpi: Share of support hours spent on the needs entrepreneurs ranked highest
measurement.baselineMethod: Session log hours compared with needs rankings
measurement.provisionalTarget: 60 percent or more of hours on top three needs

mapping.gapPattern: There are no graduation or exit rules, alumni lists are out of date, and contact stops when the programme ends.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO treats support as a one off event, so it loses track of enterprises and cannot show lasting results or use alumni as a resource.
mapping.prescription: Write graduation and exit rules, define a follow up offer for alumni with eligibility, contact alumni on a fixed schedule, and invite alumni to mentor or speak.

intervention.resources: Graduation policy template, alumni offer sheet, alumni contact log

measurement.kpi: Share of alumni of the last three cohorts contacted in the past 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Alumni list compared with the contact log

subDimensions.name: Budgeting and cost per enterprise served

mapping.gapPattern: Cost per enterprise has never been calculated, budgets exist only inside proposals, shared costs are charged to whichever grant has money, and spending is not compared with budget.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO cannot show what it costs to serve an enterprise or whether it recovers its running costs, which weakens negotiation with funders and any plan to scale.
mapping.prescription: Approve an annual budget by programme, adopt a written cost allocation method, compare spending with budget monthly, and calculate cost per enterprise from the accounts.

intervention.resources: Programme budget template, cost allocation policy template, cost per enterprise worksheet

measurement.kpi: Cost per enterprise supported calculated for each programme
measurement.baselineMethod: Accounts and participant counts for the last year
measurement.provisionalTarget: Calculated for every programme within six months

mapping.gapPattern: Books are kept in one cashbook, one person approves and makes payments, bank accounts are not reconciled, and audits are late or missing.
mapping.diagnosis: Weak accounting and payment controls expose the ESO to error and fraud and are likely to fail a funder's financial due diligence.
mapping.prescription: Set up accounting software with fund and programme codes, introduce dual payment approval, reconcile every bank and mobile money account monthly, and commission a full audit.

intervention.resources: Accounting software set up, chart of accounts with project codes, financial controls manual, audit terms of reference

measurement.kpi: Number of months in the last 12 with signed bank reconciliations
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of reconciliation files

mapping.gapPattern: Donor reports are late, leaders see no management accounts, and spending is checked against donor rules only at report time.
mapping.diagnosis: Reporting is reactive, so ineligible costs and late submissions threaten funder trust and future grants.
mapping.prescription: Create a donor reporting calendar, produce management accounts within 15 days of month end, and track spending against each donor budget with an eligibility check before payment.

intervention.resources: Reporting calendar, management accounts template, donor budget tracker

measurement.kpi: Share of donor and financial reports submitted on time in the last 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Reporting calendar compared with submission receipts

mapping.gapPattern: There are no unrestricted reserves and no cash flow forecast, so a late grant payment forces the ESO to pause delivery or stop paying staff.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO is exposed to funding timing gaps and cannot plan around them.
mapping.prescription: Build a monthly six month cash flow forecast, adopt a reserves policy, and set aside a share of every unrestricted income source until three months of core costs are covered.

intervention.resources: Cash flow forecast template, reserves policy template, unrestricted income plan

measurement.kpi: Months of core running costs covered by unrestricted reserves
measurement.baselineMethod: Bank balances divided by monthly core costs

mapping.gapPattern: One funder provides most of the income, almost nothing is multi-year or unrestricted, no income is earned, and unrelated consulting keeps the doors open.
mapping.diagnosis: Income is concentrated and short term, so the ESO follows funder priorities and cannot invest in its own mission or stay open when one grant ends.
mapping.prescription: Set diversification targets, test fees or success fees with a pilot service, seek multi-year or core grants, and ring fence consulting income for the mission with board approval.

intervention.resources: Revenue model workshop, fee pilot design, funder mapping, income tracking sheet

measurement.kpi: Share of income from the largest single funder
measurement.baselineMethod: Income by source schedule for the last financial year
measurement.provisionalTarget: Largest funder at 50 percent or less within 12 months

subDimensions.name: Investor and capital linkages for client enterprises

mapping.gapPattern: Introductions to investors and lenders are not recorded, partners appear only at pitch events, enterprises are not prepared, and finance terms are not checked.
mapping.diagnosis: Investor linkage cannot be shown to work, and unprepared or poorly screened introductions can damage the ESO's credibility and the enterprises themselves.
mapping.prescription: Keep an introduction register with outcomes, prepare each enterprise with a readiness checklist, verify claims before endorsement, and screen finance terms of partners.

intervention.resources: Introduction register, investor readiness checklist, finance partner screening criteria, partner engagement plan

measurement.kpi: Share of introductions with a recorded outcome
measurement.baselineMethod: Introduction register review
measurement.provisionalTarget: 100 percent of introductions with outcome recorded within six months

mapping.gapPattern: Partnerships are named but not written, there is no funding pipeline, funders are contacted only for reports, and grants do not cover real running costs.
mapping.diagnosis: Relationships are not managed deliberately, so funding is unpredictable and the ESO carries hidden costs.
mapping.prescription: Sign agreements with main partners, keep a monthly funding pipeline, hold a yearly review with each major funder, and apply a written running cost rate when negotiating.

intervention.resources: Partnership agreement template, funding pipeline tracker, funder meeting guide, running cost rate sheet

measurement.kpi: Share of major funders and partners with a signed agreement and a yearly review
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of agreements and meeting records
measurement.provisionalTarget: All major funders and partners covered within 12 months

mapping.gapPattern: The board meets rarely or not at all, there are no conflict of interest declarations, the director is not reviewed, and nobody could lead if the director left.
mapping.diagnosis: Governance is weak, so decisions lack oversight and the ESO is exposed to conflicts, key person risk and funder due diligence failure.
mapping.prescription: Agree a board calendar with minutes, collect annual conflict of interest declarations, run a yearly director review against targets, and write a succession plan.

intervention.resources: Board calendar and minutes templates, declaration forms, director appraisal form, succession plan template

measurement.kpi: Number of board meetings with minutes in the last 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Minute book review

mapping.gapPattern: Core staff leave within two years, there are no staff reviews, and gaps in expertise are covered by promising services the team cannot deliver.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO loses institutional knowledge and overpromises, which hurts service quality and funder confidence.
mapping.prescription: Set role descriptions and yearly reviews, plan staff development and handover notes, list skills gaps, and engage outside experts under written terms.

intervention.resources: Job description template, review form, skills gap analysis sheet, handover note template

measurement.kpi: Share of core programme staff who left in the last 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Staff register with start and end dates

mapping.gapPattern: Mentors are recruited by recommendation, have no agreement, and nobody reviews who is active or whether they help.
mapping.diagnosis: The mentor network is the main service but is not managed, so quality varies and misconduct risk is unmanaged.
mapping.prescription: Adopt written mentor selection criteria with references, a signed mentor agreement, and a yearly review of session logs and ratings with renew, coach or release decisions.

intervention.resources: Mentor selection criteria, mentor agreement template, mentor review form

measurement.kpi: Share of active mentors with a signed agreement and a reference on file
measurement.baselineMethod: Mentor files review

mapping.gapPattern: There is no safeguarding policy or complaints channel, and staff and mentors have never been trained on conduct.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO cannot protect entrepreneurs, mentors or staff from exploitation, abuse or harassment, and will fail institutional funders' safeguarding due diligence.
mapping.prescription: Adopt a board approved safeguarding policy and code of conduct, set up a confidential complaints channel explained at onboarding, and train all staff and mentors before they start.

intervention.resources: Safeguarding policy and code of conduct template, complaints procedure and case log, training pack

measurement.kpi: Share of active staff and mentors trained on safeguarding and the code of conduct
measurement.baselineMethod: Training register compared with staff and mentor lists

mapping.gapPattern: Client records sit in personal files, several spreadsheets and phones, applicants and alumni are not linked, and key fields are blank.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO cannot trace an enterprise over time or produce reliable numbers, so results claims cannot be verified.
mapping.prescription: Set up one client database with unique IDs covering applicant to alumni, write a data guide defining fields, and run a completeness check each cohort.

intervention.resources: Client database template, data dictionary, completeness checklist, staff data entry training

measurement.kpi: Share of key database fields completed for participants
measurement.baselineMethod: Database extract completeness check

mapping.gapPattern: Indicators have no baselines, nobody follows up after the programme, results are self reported and unverified, and all change is claimed as impact.
mapping.diagnosis: Reported results are not credible to funders or investors, and the ESO cannot show whether its support works.
mapping.prescription: Define indicators with baselines, follow up alumni at 12 months, verify a sample of results against documents, and state clearly how much change can be attributed.

intervention.resources: Indicator framework, follow up survey, verification checklist, attribution note template

measurement.kpi: Share of alumni followed up at 12 months with outcome data
measurement.baselineMethod: Alumni list compared with follow up records

mapping.gapPattern: Results sit in reports that no one uses, weak results are hidden, there are no review sessions, and programmes are never formally evaluated.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO does not learn from its own data, so it repeats weak practices and loses credibility with funders.
mapping.prescription: Hold a structured review after each cohort, record decisions that cite results, report missed targets to board and funders, and evaluate each major programme once per funding cycle.

intervention.resources: After cohort review template, decision log, evaluation terms of reference, peer review with another ESO

measurement.kpi: Number of decisions recorded that cite results data in the last 12 months
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of minutes and decision logs

mapping.gapPattern: Annual returns are missing, tax clearance and staff deductions are late, and the non-profit licence has lapsed.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO is exposed to penalties and cannot pass funder due diligence on legal standing.
mapping.prescription: File missing returns with the Registrar, renew the NPO licence where applicable, regularise tax and staff deductions, and keep a compliance calendar.

intervention.resources: Compliance calendar, filing checklist with Registrar, GRA and SSNIT steps

measurement.kpi: Number of statutory filings overdue
measurement.baselineMethod: Compliance calendar compared with receipts

mapping.gapPattern: The ESO holds entrepreneurs' phone numbers, business data and photos without Data Protection Commission registration, a privacy notice or security rules.
mapping.diagnosis: Entrepreneur data is exposed to misuse and the ESO breaches the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843).
mapping.prescription: Register with the Data Protection Commission, issue a plain language privacy notice with consent forms, adopt written security rules and a breach procedure, and train staff.

intervention.resources: Registration application, privacy notice and consent templates, data security policy, breach procedure

measurement.kpi: Data Protection Commission registration current (yes or no)
measurement.baselineMethod: Registration certificate check
measurement.provisionalTarget: Registered and current within three months

mapping.gapPattern: There is no risk register, funders and partners are accepted without checks, and enterprises are introduced to investors without verification.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO takes on reputational and fiduciary risk without knowing it.
mapping.prescription: Keep a risk register with owners, apply a due diligence checklist to funders and partners, and verify enterprise claims before endorsement.

intervention.resources: Risk register template, funder due diligence checklist, enterprise verification checklist

measurement.kpi: Share of new funders, partners and endorsed enterprises with a completed due diligence check
measurement.baselineMethod: Sample of checks against the list of new relationships

mapping.gapPattern: There is no anti-fraud policy, purchases are made without quotations, and incidents are handled privately.
mapping.diagnosis: Fiduciary controls are weak, and a single incident could cost funder trust and funding.
mapping.prescription: Adopt and sign an anti-fraud policy, apply written procurement rules, and set a procedure to log, investigate and report incidents to the board and funders.

intervention.resources: Anti-fraud policy template, procurement policy template, incident log

measurement.kpi: Share of staff, board members and mentors who signed the anti-fraud policy
measurement.baselineMethod: Signed acknowledgements against lists

mapping.gapPattern: Few women sit on selection panels, there is no review for gender or youth barriers, and results are never split by gender or age.
mapping.diagnosis: Inclusion claims cannot be shown, and women and young entrepreneurs may be selected less often or benefit less.
mapping.prescription: Set written targets for women and young people, review barriers each year, widen panel membership, and analyse outcomes by gender and age.

intervention.resources: Inclusion target sheet, barrier review template, disaggregated results template

measurement.kpi: Share of participants who are women and who are under 35, compared with targets
measurement.baselineMethod: Client database extract by gender and age
measurement.provisionalTarget: Targets set and reported within six months

mapping.gapPattern: Climate and environment are absent from the diagnostic, there is no screening of enterprises, and no expertise or results data exist.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO cannot respond to climate risk faced by farmers and small businesses or to funder expectations on environmental practice.
mapping.prescription: Add a climate and environmental risk check to the diagnostic, screen enterprises before endorsement, agree access to expert partners, and track adoption of climate smart practices.

intervention.resources: Climate risk check form, exclusion list, partnership with a university or specialist agency, indicator sheet

measurement.kpi: Share of enterprises completing a climate and environmental risk check
measurement.baselineMethod: Diagnostic records review

subDimensions.name: Ecosystem contribution and reach to rural and underserved enterprises

mapping.gapPattern: Activity is concentrated in the city, rural share is unknown, participants carry transport and data costs, and learning is not shared with others.
mapping.diagnosis: The ESO misses rural and underserved enterprises and does not contribute to ecosystem learning.
mapping.prescription: Plan delivery in district or community locations in local languages, track participant location, budget for transport and data support, and share tools and findings with other ESOs.

intervention.resources: Rural delivery plan, location tracking field, participant support budget, ecosystem sharing plan

measurement.kpi: Share of participants based outside the regional capital
measurement.baselineMethod: Client database location data
measurement.provisionalTarget: Share compared with written target and reviewed yearly within six months

questions.text: We can state in one sentence which entrepreneurs we serve, what problem we help them solve and what should change for them.
anchors: No agreed statement; leaders give different answers when asked separately
Target is described broadly (for example 'all SMEs') with no problem or change named
A statement exists but misses one of: who, which problem, what changes
Written statement covers who, problem and change, and two leaders give consistent answers
Board approved statement names stage, sector and area and is reflected in selection criteria and reports

evidence.requirement: Written mission or programme statement, plus separate interviews with two leaders compared with the selection criteria.

questions.text: We have a written theory of change that links our activities to the results we expect for entrepreneurs.
anchors: No written theory of change or results framework
Activities are listed in proposals but no link to expected results is shown
A theory of change exists but its links have no stated assumptions
Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions
Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions, has an indicator for each outcome and keeps a dated version history

evidence.requirement: The current theory of change or results framework and its version history.
examples: Theory of change diagram or narrative

questions.text: We have tested at least one assumption in our theory of change against our own data and changed the programme as a result.
anchors: The theory of change has not been reviewed since it was written
Reviewed informally in staff meetings with no record of changes
Reviewed once, findings noted but no programme change followed
Reviewed at least yearly using our own data, with at least one programme change recorded
Reviewed at least yearly using our own outcome data and entrepreneur views, with a programme change recorded and re-checked the following year

evidence.requirement: Review notes on the theory of change linked to a documented programme change.

questions.text: Most enterprises we supported in the last twelve months fit the target segment in our written mission or strategy.
anchors: Under 40 percent fit, or no written segment to check against
40 to 59 percent fit
60 to 74 percent fit
75 to 89 percent fit
90 percent or more fit, checked against the client database

evidence.requirement: Written target segment definition and a client database extract with stage, sector and location. The verifier counts the share that fits.
examples: Client database extract for last 12 months

questions.riskTag: Mission drift away from target segment

questions.text: Our curriculum and support are adapted to the sectors, languages and business conditions of the enterprises we serve, not imported unchanged.
anchors: Materials are imported from other programmes with no local change
Some local examples added with no input from local entrepreneurs or practitioners
Some modules adapted using staff knowledge only
Curriculum adapted with documented input from local entrepreneurs, mentors or sector practitioners
Curriculum adapted with documented local input, with local cases, language and sector data in the modules and a revision after each cohort

evidence.requirement: Curriculum files compared with the original source materials, and records of local input.
examples: Notes of consultation with entrepreneurs or sector experts

questions.text: We chose our programme length, cohort size and support intensity deliberately for the enterprises we serve, and can explain why.
anchors: Format copied from a funder or another programme with no rationale
Format set by budget or convenience; rationale given only verbally
A written rationale exists but is not linked to enterprise needs or evidence
Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage
Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage, draws on our own results or outside evidence, and the format was adjusted after a review

evidence.requirement: Programme design note explaining length, cohort size and intensity, and any later adjustment.

questions.text: Our programme design includes scheduled peer learning among entrepreneurs in the same cohort.
anchors: No peer learning; entrepreneurs meet only staff or mentors one to one
Entrepreneurs meet at events but no peer sessions are planned
Peer sessions are held occasionally, without structure or records
Peer sessions are scheduled in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records
Peer sessions run in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records, and entrepreneur feedback on them is collected and used to adjust later sessions

evidence.requirement: Programme schedule showing peer sessions, with attendance records and feedback.

questions.text: We design new programmes around what target entrepreneurs tell us they need, not only around what funders offer to pay for.
anchors: Programmes are designed only to match funder calls
Entrepreneurs are consulted informally after the design is fixed
Needs were gathered for some programmes but not written up
A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years
A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years, and a funded activity was reshaped or declined because it did not fit their needs

evidence.requirement: Needs assessments or survey results dated before programme design, and an example of a design change driven by them.

questions.text: We know which other organisations serve the same enterprises in our area and how our offer differs from theirs.
anchors: We do not know what other providers do
Leaders can name a few providers but have not compared offers
A list of providers exists but is out of date or lacks offer details
Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months
Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months, and our positioning and referral choices use the gaps and overlaps it shows

evidence.requirement: Provider mapping or ecosystem map with a review date, and examples of referrals or positioning decisions based on it.

questions.text: We have an estimate of how many enterprises fit our target segment in our area and the share of them we reach each year.
anchors: No estimate of the target population
Rough figure quoted from memory with no source
Estimate taken from a published or partner source but no reach share worked out
Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months
Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months, with reach share tracked yearly by area or sector and used to set targets

evidence.requirement: A document showing the population estimate, its source and the reach calculation.

questions.text: We have a written strategic plan with measurable targets that leaders review at least once a year.
anchors: No written plan
The plan is a funding proposal or concept note only
A written plan exists but has no measurable targets or is over three years old
A plan under three years old has measurable targets and was reviewed in the last 12 months
A board approved plan under three years old has measurable targets, a budget linked to them, a review in the last 12 months and an annual progress report

evidence.requirement: Current strategic plan and the latest annual review.

questions.text: Our programme delivery model is written down well enough that a trained new team or a new location could run it.
anchors: The model exists only in the heads of founders or key staff
Slide decks or proposals describe the model but give no operating steps
Some processes are documented with major gaps in selection, delivery or follow up
A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection
A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection, and two teams or sites have used it with documented adjustments

evidence.requirement: Operating manual or standard procedures, and evidence of use by someone other than its authors.
examples: Notes from a second team or site using it

questions.riskTag: Delivery model not documented for scale

questions.text: Before adding cohorts, locations or programmes, we check that we have enough staff, mentors and funding to keep quality.
anchors: Expansion is decided when funding is offered, without a capacity check
Leaders discuss capacity informally
Capacity is checked for finance only
A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision
A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision, quality indicators are tracked afterwards and growth is paused if they fall

evidence.requirement: Expansion decision notes showing a capacity check, and quality data after the last expansion.

questions.text: We select enterprises using written criteria that at least two reviewers score independently.
anchors: Selection is by one person or personal contact, with no written criteria
Criteria are understood informally and one person decides
Written criteria exist but are not shared with applicants or not scored consistently
Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet
Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet, score differences are discussed, decisions are minuted and criteria are reviewed after each round

evidence.requirement: Selection criteria, completed scoring sheets from at least two reviewers, and selection minutes for the last round.

questions.text: We keep a record of every applicant at every stage, with the reason for each selection or rejection.
anchors: No application records are kept beyond selected enterprises
Applications sit in email or paper files and are not collated
A list of applicants and outcomes exists without reasons
A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision
A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision, and the data is analysed, for example by comparing selected with rejected applicants

evidence.requirement: Applicant database or register for the last round, including rejected applicants.
examples: Analysis of selected versus rejected applicants

questions.text: We can show that we reach entrepreneurs who would not otherwise be supported, not only those already funded or well connected.
anchors: Most participants were already funded or supported elsewhere, or this is not recorded
Participants come mainly from leaders' own networks
Some outreach beyond networks, but no data on prior support
Application form records prior support, and at least half of participants had received none
Application form records prior support and at least half of participants had none, results are compared for those with and without prior support, and outreach is adjusted

evidence.requirement: Application data on prior support and the outreach plan.
examples: Application form with prior support question
Share of participants with no prior support

questions.text: Each selected enterprise receives a baseline diagnostic that leads to a written support plan within 30 days of starting.
anchors: Under 20 percent of the last cohort, or no baseline diagnostic is used
20 to 49 percent
50 to 74 percent
75 to 94 percent
95 percent or more, with support plans on file

evidence.requirement: Diagnostic forms and support plans for the last cohort with dates. The verifier counts those done within 30 days.

questions.riskTag: No baseline diagnostic or support plan

questions.text: Most of our support time goes to the needs entrepreneurs rank highest, such as sales, finance access or hiring, not mainly to pitch preparation.
anchors: Support is mostly pitch decks and general workshops; needs are never asked
Needs are asked at entry but support follows a fixed curriculum
Some modules adapt to stated needs, and time use is not tracked
Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked
Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked, needs are re-ranked mid programme and support is re-planned where they changed

evidence.requirement: Needs ranking from entrepreneurs and a session or time log showing where support hours went.

questions.riskTag: Support not matched to entrepreneur needs

questions.text: Entrepreneur feedback on mentors and sessions leads to documented changes in how we deliver.
anchors: No feedback is collected
Informal comments are heard but nothing is recorded
Feedback forms are collected but not analysed
Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made
Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made, changes are reported back to entrepreneurs and ratings are tracked across cohorts

evidence.requirement: Feedback forms or survey results and the change record that followed.
examples: Change log or minutes citing feedback

questions.text: Each entrepreneur is matched to a mentor or coach using a written view of the entrepreneur's needs and the mentor's expertise.
anchors: Mentors are assigned by availability or personal contact, with no assessment
Staff match by judgement and give no written reasons
Matches are recorded but based only on sector, not on need
Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, and the entrepreneur may ask for a change
Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, the entrepreneur may ask for a change, match quality is tracked and mismatches are corrected within 30 days

evidence.requirement: Match records for the last cohort and mentor profiles.

questions.text: Market access support, such as buyer introductions or market information, is a deliberate part of our offer with named activities.
anchors: No market access support is offered
Occasional introductions happen when staff happen to know a buyer
Market access sessions are included with no buyer or channel partner involved
Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part
Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part, and sales or contracts that result are tracked for participating enterprises

evidence.requirement: Programme plan showing market access activities, buyer participation records and any sales tracking.
examples: Contracts or orders recorded after linkage

questions.riskTag: Market access not part of the offer

questions.text: We have written criteria and a process for graduating, pausing or exiting enterprises from our programmes.
anchors: No graduation or exit rules; enterprises drift
Practice is informal and decided case by case
Criteria are written for graduation only
Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise
Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise, decisions are recorded and exited enterprises get a closing review and referral

evidence.requirement: Graduation and exit policy plus decision records for the last cohort.

questions.text: We were in contact with most alumni of our last three cohorts during the past twelve months.
anchors: Under 20 percent contacted, or there is no alumni list
20 to 39 percent contacted
40 to 59 percent contacted
60 to 79 percent contacted
80 percent or more contacted, with contact dates recorded

evidence.requirement: Alumni list with dated contact records. The verifier calculates the share contacted in the last 12 months.
examples: Alumni database with last contact date

anchors: No support is offered after the programme ends
Alumni can call staff for informal help
Follow-up events are held occasionally for all alumni
A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member
A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member, is adjusted by alumni stage, and its uptake and outcomes are recorded

consistencyChecks.rule: An ESO that says it reaches people who would not otherwise be supported should know where its participants are based.
Following up alumni for outcomes needs records that link applicants, participants and alumni.
On time donor reports usually need accounts coded by donor fund. Check the reporting is not built on manual rework.
A strong safeguarding policy with almost nobody trained suggests the policy is on paper only.
Data Protection Commission registration with no security rules or breach procedure suggests registration is a formality.
Baselines for every participant need complete data fields. If fields are mostly blank, the baseline claim needs checking.
A cost per enterprise that includes shared costs needs a written method for sharing them.
Claiming to test the theory of change against data while holding no review after cohorts is inconsistent.
Entrepreneur feedback that leads to changes should also reach mentor management. Check mentors are reviewed.
Analysis of outcomes by gender and age depends on complete gender and age fields in the database.
